classifications.mutant: adapters/peer-http/src/remote.rs:224:17: delete field health from struct PeerRegistryStatus expression in PeerRegistry::status
classifications.explanation: This fallback requires poisoning the private status mutex. Every holder only moves or clones owned validated identifiers, strings, and primitive diagnostic fields; no caller callback, clock, adapter, network operation, or fallible formatter runs while this guard is held. Allocation failure aborts rather than unwinding. Supported registry operations therefore cannot poison this mutex; ordinary disconnected and failed-connection health remain independently tested.

The mutation joins only the authority and attempt-revision comparisons. ExecutionAuthorityEstablished is one-shot before start, so the authority basis cannot change here. revision_for_attempt is derived from the current node-execution projection; a changed or retired revision therefore also changes the independently compared execution (or attempt), and that earlier disjunction still rejects the ticket.

The mutation joins only the lease and authority comparisons. Authority is immutable after start. Under the supported worker protocol, a heartbeat is reported only after the adapter-entry decision, so a concurrent renewal also changes the independently compared attempt. Recovery expires a lease together with recovery classification of its attempt, and replacement changes attempt admission facts. A lease-only change during pre-entry preparation has no supported reporting path; the defensive original guard is retained.

The mutation joins only the execution and lease comparisons. A cancellation-only execution change is also refused by cancellation_reason_for_execution on the refreshed head. Revision changes are independently checked through revision_for_attempt; output/terminal/recovery transitions also change the independently compared attempt. An otherwise isolated execution change that could authorize a new entry cannot be produced by a valid active-attempt history.

The mutation joins only the attempt and execution comparisons. An execution-only cancellation still meets the following refreshed cancellation check. An attempt-only observation requires an already recorded adapter-entry decision, or terminal/recovery state; folding the final CapabilityAdapterEntryDecisionRecorded rejects a duplicate, terminal, or retired candidate before the prepared handle can enter. Immutable request coordinates cannot change independently under a valid history; lease, authority, and revision comparisons remain disjunctions.

The loaded projection's run identity is fixed by its keyed journal. A valid RunCreated binds its workflow to its exact stored revision, and no later event can change that workflow. The separate immutable creation-revision comparison therefore already rejects a foreign workflow. An existing child with the expected creation revision but a different workflow cannot arise through valid creation or prospective reconciliation. The independent same-workflow/different-creation-pin refusal test catches weakening the adjacent creation check.
